scope: The terminal command, installed agent skills, local Product Report, coverage reviews and Blueprint movement between repositories.
method: Static inspection of the repository's instructions, documentation, CLI source, bundled agent skills, report viewer, local host, supporting tests, fixtures, configuration and maintenance scripts.
Command behavior traced from `src/cli.ts` through each command implementation into the core parsing, portability, installation, and local-server modules.
Skill behavior traced from each `SKILL.md` and its references; the repository's docs and specs were used as leads and confirmed against implementation.
What each Step does to the things the product keeps, and who may, read from the format contract and the structural rules that enforce it.
Supporting files were considered for their effect on modeled behavior; development tooling and test examples do not automatically become Product capabilities.
Source areas locate broad inspection context. Exact considered files and their conclusions belong to the latest completed review in this Coverage document, not to a directory-wide completeness claim.
Source inspection did not execute the target application, tests, build or package scripts; structural lint used the isolated BusinessLens CLI.

exclusions.description: The public Nuxt layers and JavaScript entry points for third-party hosts are deliberately outside this model’s scope.
The visual identity — palette, type, approved surfaces, logo and icon family — and shared background experiments are deliberately outside this model’s scope.
Installing skills through the Claude plugin marketplace is deliberately outside this model’s scope.

limitations: The model describes established behavior found by reading source; it makes no claim that behavior is currently correct, released, or verified.
Provider detection paths and the harness invocation syntaxes are recorded as the product's own claims; no harness was run to confirm them.
Catalog and GitHub interactions were read from source only. No network call was made.
rationale:
The model describes the terminal command, installed agent skills, local Product
Report, coverage reviews and Blueprint movement between repositories.
Public hosting contracts, visual identity and Claude plugin marketplace
installation are explicit model exclusions. Operating the external Blueprint
catalog remains outside the Product boundary. The model is under review; its
status does not claim that a Coverage review has been completed.

entries.summary: Read public dispatch, argument validation, model working-directory handling, output/exit behavior and package version resolution. The CLI exposes install, update, lint, view, assessment and Blueprint commands. Assessment commands emit JSON and do not write model meaning. Updated the CLI model summary to include this existing public surface.

Traced capture, exact-file fingerprints, no-symlink traversal, ignored-input policy, pending/completed lifecycle, atomic worktree-local storage, conclusion replacement and link validation. Completion requires all inputs accounted for, unchanged sources and a structurally valid final model. Status derives later additions, modifications, deletions, unreadability and policy changes without advancing the baseline. The Product checks record consistency, not whether an agent actually understood a file. No local baseline exists in a new clone; model files are fingerprinted separately.

Read provider registry and detection, interactive/default/explicit selection, project/global destinations, ownership marker validation, preflight installation refusal, safe replacement and managed update discovery. These implement skill distribution without creating a Product Model. Corrected the installation Scenario to describe printed scope and --yes defaults accurately; retired managed skills are removed but not individually reported. Provider harnesses were not executed.

Inspected resource discovery, compact/expanded ownership, schema-10 loading, YAML and Markdown sections, typed Steps, Entity facts/states/relations, Context identifiers, Rule grants, Reference grammar and root selection. Coverage keeps Scope, approved Exclusions and known Unmapped behavior distinct. These support modeled resources and structural inspection; Source areas and navigation references cannot substitute for exact-file assessment.

Traced structural error/warning handling, identifier/reference resolution, Context and Actor compatibility, coverage requirements, Step state continuity and permission selection. Read the shared grant evaluator: it rejects impossible actors/closed operations and checks state compatibility; it does not evaluate target runtime authorization or prove semantic alignment. Lint is read-only and returns JSON findings and counts when requested.

Traced workspace compilation, schema-15 resource fields and relations, portable projection, canonical digests, safe generated output, staged expansion, lint-before-replacement and explicit-force backups. Projection removes repository-navigation fields, source/exclusion/gap paths and local assessment data; authored prose and Method remain until expansion replaces Method. Corrected Blueprint and export wording to describe semantic preservation and the exact redaction boundary, not byte identity or automatic removal of origin statements.

Read catalog-name/origin validation, anonymous requests, redirect and response size limits, media-type/schema/identity/digest checks, optional safe logo retrieval and canonical expansion. The source distinguishes missing, withdrawn and unavailable Blueprints. These support the pull Scenarios; no external catalog or network behavior was exercised.

Traced Git context/provenance helpers and contribution from authenticated gh preflight through lint, public metadata checks, portable canonical expansion, confirmation, temporary fork/clone, command-owned branch replacement and new/existing pull request reporting. Corrected the missing-metadata Scenario: metadata failures are reported first, logo separately after they pass. External GitHub behavior and credentials were not exercised; source repository branch/remotes are not mutated by contribution.

Read structural gate before server startup, loopback binding/Host checks, static report and asset routes, read-only repository inventory/assessment context, debounced model watch, SSE revisions, last-valid report retention and shutdown. Status refresh reads local assessment state without creating or advancing it. This review used source evidence, not target server execution.

Read Product-logo location, regular-file and size restrictions, UTF-8/XML parsing, inert SVG allowlists, namespace checks and prohibition of external or active content. Validation supports local viewing and Blueprint logo handling. The separate exported JavaScript logo-validation API is within the existing public-host contract exclusion; this mixed file still supports in-scope CLI behavior.

entries.summary: Read third-party attribution and license texts as supporting distribution material for Diagram Design inspiration, Vue Flow and the separately loaded ELK worker. These files carry notices rather than independent Product behavior. Their presence was considered; this accounting makes no legal-compliance determination.

Inspected the neutral Product-logo SVG and shared report CSS. The assets establish bounded viewport/pane scrolling, row and Step presentation, responsive single-column rows, resource marks, topology/table overflow and focus affordances. These are supporting presentation inputs for the local report; source inspection establishes their declared rules without claiming rendered visual correctness.

Traced About/Coverage/References rendering and local repository accounting. Authored Product/Coverage fields retain their labels; current paths, exact annotations, completed and pending assessments and file comparisons remain separate. The loader is read-only; refresh cannot complete assessment. Without a baseline, Unassessed means no completed historical accounting. Selected files expose recorded outcome, summary, model resource paths, exclusions and gaps; missing/failed inventory preserves authored paths and unlocated entries. Parents aggregate counts and do not confer assessment on children.

Read tree construction and filtering: live inventory, comparison paths, pending worklist paths, authored source/gap/exclusion paths and local References are inserted independently; removed paths therefore remain selectable. Ancestors aggregate distinct annotation IDs and comparison counts, unannotated one-child paths may be compressed, and string filtering retains ancestor context. No path acquires a reviewed outcome from a source-area parent or Reference.

Traced report projection, six collection rail entries and three cross-collection views, Overview tabs, resource-page ownership, search-by-title/description/ID, facet filtering, Rows/Graph controls and state persistence. The Resource collection Screen was corrected to describe the existing shared Rows/Graph toolbar and populated filter axes. Confirmed a separate unresolved implementation mismatch: multiple chosen values are summarized in one per-axis chip and clearing that chip removes the axis, despite the model promising individually removable selected-value chips. Read-only UI state changes do not edit model files.

Read URL serialization and browser-local reading preferences. Navigation binds section/resource/tab/topology selections, per-reading scroll/graph state is restored when possible, removed model IDs are pruned, and row-count choices use a per-collection cookie. The navigation composable still carries r/rc route-window state but active Scenario cards do not consume it; this does not establish a currently available route selector. Width observation only selects responsive presentation.

Inspected collection subject filtering, resource row presentation, Domain/Interface Nuxt UI tree cards and toolbar chips. Graph subjects come from the same facet-filtered collection; focus adds a graph neighbourhood; row cards show summaries and relations and tree children navigate separately from expansion. Domain cards retain unassigned resources. The filter chip component emits one removal per supplied chip; the shell supplies one chip per axis, an explicitly retained discrepancy against per-value-chip intent.

Read collection/row/fact projections for every resource type. Domain and Interface cards derive child resources from classification and containment; ordinary rows expose kind-specific identifying metrics. Filters derive offered axes from row presentation, combine selections with OR within an axis and AND across axes, and Domain grouping/Actor-first grouping preserve unassigned resources. These modules summarize model relations rather than inspect implementation correctness.

Traced resource page Overview blocks, Scenarios/Lifecycle peers, authored body fields, resource connections, Interface delivery, Experience shared Screens, Context breadcrumbs, references and escaped prose rendering. Resource pages use stable keys and parent ownership. Active Scenario URLs are redirected into their parent card list; the older route-window renderer in ResourceBody is not the active Scenario path. Resource links and source references support navigation but are not verification evidence. No account, mutation or publish operation was found in these UI components.

Read page-tab/block selection, resource ownership and named destinations, incoming/outgoing connection derivation, documentation routing and the constrained Markdown renderer. Capability/Journey pages have Scenarios and Entities with States have Lifecycle; Scenarios resolve to their mandatory parent. Markdown escapes authored HTML before restoring recognized formatting and only permits HTTP(S) prose links. Connections preserve model relationships and distinguish derived reach.

Inspected the active Scenario card path. Cards present Trigger/Outcome and ending Entity effects, then expand Intent, ordered Steps, Actor/Product identity, Entity effect phrases, all Context breadcrumbs, Journey Step Capabilities, decisions and edge cases. Confirmed unresolved visibility gaps: this path does not render Scenario supportingContent or References, and Where iterates contexts without displaying authored route names, so equal places on differently named routes cannot be distinguished by those labels. The obsolete model claim of choosing/restoring a route window was corrected to describe card expansion. These known issues are not treated as missing model scope or proof of full UI alignment.

Read per-report/parent Scenario card expansion persistence: known keys are restored from app memory/session storage, direct Scenario selection opens the matching card, removed keys are pruned, and denied/malformed storage leaves reading usable. This supports card expansion persistence; it does not implement route selection or composition windows.

Read shared Step Actor/Capability resolution and route-window capacity/clamping functions. Actor lookup and Journey-only Step Capability lookup feed the active cards. Route-window helpers remain in the older ResourceBody renderer; their presence alone does not establish route controls in the current card reading.

Traced the typed Product Report projection and its principal relations: qualified Context resolution, complete Product/Coverage passthrough, resource fields and support sections/references, Capability/Journey effects, ending states, Entity lifecycle arcs, Rule targets/grants and resource indexes. No repository assessment or live inventory is inferred from this portable model projection. Scenario routes/supporting sections/references survive this projection, so their absence in the active card reading is a rendering issue. These source-level derivations were inspected without running a report or treating relation counts as semantic completeness.

Traced Compare delivery, What changes what and Rule attachments matrices, per-view focus/type controls, column windowing and resource/evidence links. Cells come only from authored model relations. Confirmed unresolved explanatory mismatch: the delivery table caption says an empty cell means the Interface does not deliver it, while the named-view contract only supports absence of an authored delivery Context; no runtime absence was established.

Read all fixed view definitions and their derivations: Product-rooted Interface containment, Domain/Capability/Journey/Rule reach occurrences, authored Entity relations, delivery and mutation matrices and exact Rule attachment selectors. Focus preserves one-hop connections and focused containment descendants; URL state is validated against current resources; direct attachments remain distinct from inherited reach. Reads are excluded from mutations and disconnected Entities remain in relationship input. These are model-derived readings, not claims that repository behavior agrees.

Read lifecycle rendering from projected States and Step arcs, including creation/removal, unreached states, grants/restrictions, forbidden arcs and the full textual arc reading beneath the diagram. Information changes without stated state transitions remain listed when not drawable. No execution or permission enforcement was inferred from the rendered Rule sentences.

Read lifecycle graph construction: named States become nodes; explicit Step endpoints create edges; nondrawable information changes stay outside the machine; creation/removal terminals are added only when used; applicable prohibitions and Rule restriction markers are retained. The source code composes existing model assertions rather than checking real-world lifecycle or permissions.

Traced diagram measurement, Product-rooted tree placement or cancellable ELK-worker arrangement, complete fallback nodes/relationships when layout fails, branch expansion, resource opening and non-editable Vue Flow nodes. Browser-local viewport state supports zoom/pan restoration and resizing retains the visible center. Hover changes emphasis, not geometry. The source implements reading affordances; no screenshots, live browser or graph execution were used to certify visual results.

Read dependency-free diagram data/projection adapters, ELK input/output conversion and worker bootstrap, plus measured contour-based tree layout with orthogonal branch routes. These files arrange a previously derived model graph and do not add Product relations or inspect repository source.

Read contextual term definitions, searchable/browsable vocabulary, links between definitions and their documentation, return-focus handling and the tooltips show/hide/undo controls. Definitions are sourced from the generated registry and UI preferences are browser-local, with no Product Model write.

Read the cookie-backed term-tooltip preference and shared vocabulary panel state, including an origin element ID for focus restoration. Hiding teaching affordances retains the vocabulary panel as the way to restore them. These preferences do not change authored meaning.

Read vocabulary addressing/search/grouping and the generated term registry structure and definitions. Terms link to owning documentation pages, mentions are precomputed text ranges, Scenario words retain their owner, and search ranks name/alias before definition matches. The generated registry is supporting explanatory data; it does not create model resources.

Inspected the complete local accounting protocol: capture tracked and nonignored untracked source inputs, record exact-path reviewed/excluded/uncertain conclusions, validate resource and Coverage links, finish only against unchanged sources and a structurally valid final model, retain worktree-local history and compare later source/model changes. No baseline means unknown inspection history, not an absent model. The CLI lifecycle and the agent adoption handoffs are represented in the updated model.

Read Product identity/narrative/limitations, co-located asset rules, optional Reference kinds and roles, code target grammar and tracking, Screen-state annotations and portable profiles.
